pageInfo.subtitle: Develop effortless left-hand hammer-on velocity, micro-plucking pull-offs, symmetrical trills, and fluid multi-octave lines.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Legato (meaning 'tied together' in Italian) creates seamless, liquid musical sentences where notes flow into one another without the sharp percussive attack of the pick. While alternate picking delivers machine-gun staccato bite, legato provides vocal, saxophone-like smoothness and blistering speed with almost zero right-hand effort. Championed by icons like Allan Holdsworth, Joe Satriani, Shawn Lane, and Richie Kotzen, true legato mastery requires building independent fretting-hand hammer-on velocity, micro-plucking pull-off mechanics, and two-hand muting discipline.

guidelines.title: The Biomechanics of Liquid Legato Playing

items.text: The Hammer Strike Velocity: Hammer-on power comes from acceleration, not brute clamping force; strike the string right behind the fret wire like a piano hammer.
The Micro-Pluck Pull-Off: Never lift your finger straight up; pull off slightly downward with a tiny micro-pluck to re-energize the string for the underlying note.
Pre-Fretting the Lower Note: When executing a pull-off, the receiving lower finger must already be firmly planted on its fret before the higher finger releases.
Pinky Independence Conditioning: The 4th finger naturally lacks extensor tendon independence; dedicate daily isolated trills to strengthen the 3rd and 4th finger pair.
Thumb Center Alignment: Anchor your fretting thumb squarely behind the middle of the neck, keeping the palm from collapsing against the bottom edge of the fretboard.
The Pick As Ignition Switch: Pick only the first note on each string change to ignite the string's vibration, allowing hammer-ons and pull-offs to generate all subsequent notes.
Hammer-On From Nowhere: When descending to a lower string, hammer your finger directly onto the string without picking to achieve true unbroken legato flow.
3NPS Symmetrical Finger Grids: 3-note-per-string patterns create predictable finger groupings (1-2-4 or 1-3-4) that allow your fretting hand to motor through scales effortlessly.
Slide-Legato Connectors: Use quick index-finger or pinky slides to transition between positions without interrupting the legato stream.
Two-Hand Sympathetic Muting: Rest your picking-hand palm across lower unplayed strings and use the underside of your fretting index finger to mute higher strings.

exercises.title: Hammer-On Velocity Calibration (1-2 and 1-3 Pairs)
exercises.description: Before playing rapid multi-finger runs, calibrate your hammer-on attack. Pick the initial note cleanly, then strike the second note with pure fretting-hand velocity. The hammered note should match the picked note in volume, punch, and tonal clarity across strings 1, 2, 3, and 4.

patternNote.text: Pick once per pair: [5 ➔ 7] Index to Ring | [5 ➔ 8] Index to Pinky

notation.title: Hammer-On Velocity Calibration Across Strings 1-4
notation.staveTitle: Calibrating Equal Acoustic Volume Between Picked and Hammered Notes

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Do not squeeze your thumb into the back of the neck. Think of your fingers as quick piano hammers dropping from above. Clean hammer-on volume comes from velocity, not grip strength.

exercises.title: The Micro-Pluck Pull-Off Dynamics
exercises.description: Lifting your finger straight up results in a weak, dying note. To produce a singing pull-off, execute a subtle downward 'micro-pluck' with the releasing fingertip, slightly plucking the string as you pull away. Ensure your index finger is pre-planted firmly on fret 5 before pulling off.

patternNote.text: Pull-Off Geometry: Pre-plant index on fret 5 ➔ Micro-pluck downward with pinky (8) or ring (7)

notation.title: Micro-Pluck Pull-Off Mechanics
notation.staveTitle: Isolating Continuous Pull-Off Volume and Articulation

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Listen to the tone: a proper micro-pluck sounds crisp and percussive, almost as if you used a pick. Keep your wrist completely relaxed.

exercises.title: The Symmetrical 4-Note Trill Loop
exercises.description: Continuous trills build the muscle endurance, tendon independence, and timing consistency needed for professional legato playing. Pick only the very first note, then let your fretting hand maintain an unbroken 16th-note motor across frets 5-7-8-7 across strings 1, 2, 3, and 4.

patternNote.text: Endless Motor: [5 ➔ 7 ➔ 8 ➔ 7] repeated continuously without re-picking

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how your middle and pinky fingers fatigue faster than your index and ring fingers. If you feel lactic acid burn, drop your arm to your side, shake it out, and restart at a lower tempo.

exercises.title: 3-Note-Per-String Ascending Legato Cascade
exercises.description: 3-note-per-string scales are custom-built for legato. With exactly 3 notes on every string, you strike only the first note with your pick, hammering the remaining two notes. This study traverses A Dorian from string 6 all the way to string 1, reversing into a silky descending cascade.

patternNote.text: 1 Pick Per String: Strike first note ➔ Hammer-on next 2 notes with fretting hand

notation.title: 3-Note-Per-String A Dorian Legato Cascade
notation.staveTitle: High-Speed 3NPS Legato Traversing All Six Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how little your right hand has to do. Focus all your attention on fret-hand finger curvature and keeping unplayed strings silent with your palm.

exercises.title: Descending Hammer-On from Nowhere
exercises.description: True legato virtuosos (like Allan Holdsworth and Shawn Lane) descend strings without picking at all. When transitioning from string 1 to string 2, your pinky or ring finger strikes the new string from thin air ('hammer-on from nowhere') with enough velocity to produce a loud, clean note without pick assistance.

patternNote.text: Zero-Pick String Shifts: Descend strings using pure fretting-hand hammer strikes

notation.title: Descending Hammer-On from Nowhere Drill
notation.staveTitle: Pure Fretting-Hand Descending Cascades Without Pick Assistance

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Try playing this exercise with your right hand behind your back! Generating full volume purely from your left hand is the ultimate test of finger velocity.

exercises.title: The Satriani Sliding Legato Highway
exercises.description: Joe Satriani revolutionized legato by combining hammer-ons with lightning-fast finger slides along single strings. In this study, you hammer through three notes, slide your pinky up two frets, pull off downward, and slide your index finger back down, creating an endless singing ribbon of sound.

patternNote.text: Satriani Hybrid: Hammer-on ➔ Slide to next position ➔ Pull-off ➔ Slide return

notation.title: Sliding Legato Position Shifts
notation.staveTitle: High-Speed Linear Position Transitions via Legato Finger Slides

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Maintain constant fretboard contact during the slide. The slide should sound completely connected, with no pause or stutter between the fret positions.

exercises.title: The Master Legato Etude: Liquid Holdsworth Lines
exercises.description: This culminating 4-measure etude synthesizes all legato principles: rapid 3NPS cascades, hammer-ons from nowhere across string changes, position-shifting slides, and singing vocal vibrato over Am7 - D9 - Fmaj7 - Em7. Play with total physical relaxation and buttery smoothness.

patternNote.text: Complete Synthesis: 3NPS Cascades + Unpicked String Shifts + Linear Slides + Vocal Vibrato

notation.title: Master Liquid Legato Etude
notation.staveTitle: Comprehensive 4-Bar Liquid Legato Etude Across Am7 - D9 - Fmaj7 - Em7

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use a neck pickup with moderate gain or a smooth overdrive pedal. The notes should sound like an uninterrupted vocal line or a saxophone phrase, with no percussive pick clicks.

tips.title: Legato Mastery Insights, Pitfalls & Daily Workout

items.title: 3 Mistakes That Kill Legato Playing
items: Lifting Straight Off on Pull-Offs: Simply taking your finger off the fret produces a quiet, muffled note. You must execute a micro-pluck downward to keep the string vibrating.
Brute Clamping Force: Squeezing the back of the neck with your thumb causes instant forearm fatigue and destroys speed. Power comes from quick finger velocity, not vice-grip pressure.
Uncontrolled String Noise: Because your right hand isn't picking each note, open strings can ring out wildly. You must keep your right-hand palm resting on lower strings at all times.

items.title: Masters of Legato Playing
items: Allan Holdsworth: The peerless pioneer of four-finger stretch legato; floated through complex chord changes with saxophone-like sheets of liquid notes.
Joe Satriani: Mastered the singing, accessible side of legato; famous for high-speed linear slides, whammy bar scoops, and vocal blues-rock phrasing.
Shawn Lane: Regarded as having the fastest, most effortless fretting-hand legato in guitar history, executing multi-octave descending runs with zero pick attack.
Richie Kotzen: Virtuosic fusion and rock powerhouse who completely abandoned picks to play blistering, expressive legato lines entirely with his bare hands.

items.title: The 15-Minute Daily Legato Workout
items: Block 1: Isolated 2-Finger Trill Cycles (5 min) - Spend 90 seconds each on index-middle (1-2), index-ring (1-3), and ring-pinky (3-4) trills at 75 BPM.
Block 2: 3NPS Unbroken Scales (5 min) - Traverse 3NPS major and minor scales, picking only once per string and focusing on seamless string transitions.
Block 3: Linear Sliding Bursts (5 min) - Practice the Satriani slide sequence along strings 1 and 2, maximizing velocity and keeping unplayed strings completely muted.
